title: [finding] `checklist-test` SKILL.md spells the model ladder beside the instrument it tells the reader to quote, and its ceiling names a model that no longer exists
body:
Filed by the `domain:spec` seat 4 (`session_01AmH9bKvGoLjiY86Q4Z3og2`, seat post #18917) on 2026-09-21, from the `out_of_scope_findings` of the dev delivering #19544 / PR #19573. ⛔ Filed unassigned, ⛔ no `priority:*`, ⛔ no type — routing and grading are triage's. ⛔ Not a claim. ⛔ Not a ruling.

## The defect

`.claude/skills/checklist-test/SKILL.md` tells a reader to take the model tier from the instrument rather than from memory — and then spells the ladder **beside** it, ending in a model that **no longer exists**:

> 派发 runner 子代理时,档位引当次 `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --tier <paths>` 的输出、⛔ 不凭记忆(floor sonnet · default opus · **ceiling fable**)

⭐ The sentence is **self-refuting once #19573 lands**: it orders the reader to quote the instrument, and the instrument will print a ceiling **derived from `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`**, which #19573 moves to opus. The parenthetical then contradicts the very output it points at, and it names a tier that answers HTTP 429 「You've reached your Fable limit」 to anyone who tries it.

## ⏱️ Measured by this seat before filing, ⛔ not adopted from the dev's report

| reading | value |
| --- | --- |
| occurrences of the retired family word in that file | **1** |
| the file's length, as the control that the grep had somewhere to look | **238** lines |
| what the instrument will print after #19573 | a ceiling **derived** from the constant, ⛔ not a literal written beside it |
| the same stale parenthetical elsewhere | already repaired in `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` by PR #19573 |

## Why it was not fixed where it was found

PR #19573's declared file surface is `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` and `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/`. This file is neither. ⚠️ It **is** `.claude/**` and therefore the same **Tier S**, so it could have ridden along — the dev stopped at its declared surface instead of widening silently, which is what the dispatch told it to do. ⛔ Recorded rather than quietly absorbed.

## What a fix looks like

⭐ The repair #19573 used is the better one and should be copied rather than re-invented: **derive the ceiling instead of writing it**. If the line must stay prose, then it names no model at all and points only at the instrument's output — a ladder written beside an instrument is a second copy that will go stale again the next time a tier moves, which is exactly what happened here.

⚠️ Whoever takes it should sweep for the same shape rather than fixing one line: this is the **second** carrier of that parenthetical found in two days.

## 查重词

`checklist-test ceiling fable` · `ladder retired tier skill text` · `contract review tier opus` · `floor sonnet default opus` · `档位引当次输出 不凭记忆`
---

## ⭐ Added after the at-tier review of PR #19573 — the fix must be WIDER than one line

The independent reviewer of #19573 measured something this card did not know when it was filed, and it changes the deliverable:

> the new `RETIRED_TIER_WORDS` guard's radius will **never** reach it (renderings only; the id scan is rooted at `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch` and the line spells no id). Nothing else in the tree reads that file's ladder text.

⇒ ⛔ **Fixing the line alone leaves the hole that produced it.** PR #19573 landed a guard that catches a retired tier word in the renderings and under `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/`. This file is in neither radius, and it spells the family word **without an id**, so even an id scan would miss it.

**The deliverable is therefore two things in one round:**

1. repair the line — ⭐ preferably by **deriving** the ceiling the way #19573 did, ⛔ not by writing a fresh literal that goes stale the next time a tier moves; and
2. **widen the retired-word scan across `.claude/skills/**` prose**, so the next stale ladder is caught by the instrument rather than by a reviewer who happened to look.

⚠️ Pin the widening with a case that fails when a `.claude/skills/**` file gains the retired family word, and prove it fires — a guard whose radius is wrong is precisely what this card is about.

## Also owed in the same round — a provenance line, ⛔ not a rule change

The same review found that PR #19573's new docblock renders 「改成 opus」 as a quotation whose only trace is **the owning seat's own claim comment**, not a maintainer-authored artifact. The maintainer's verbatim words on the record are 「fable 没有了」; the choice of opus was their ruling, given to the seat in conversation, and the card body marks only the verbatim half.

⛔ No rule was breached and ⛔ nothing there is false — but rules text that attributes words should say where they came from. Attribute it as a seat-relayed ruling with its date, rather than leaving it to read as a maintainer-authored quotation.
